tool.title: Build the docs site locally
tool.description: Build the published site on this machine, so a page can be looked at rather than described: the same Jekyll build `pages-publish` runs in CI, into a directory of your choosing, and never pushed. The local half of the two site builds: local and GitHub builds are two Tools for one skill.

inputs.name: dest
inputs.description: Where to write the built site. Default: a temporary directory.

outputs.name: site
outputs.description: The built site, as `pages-publish` would publish it.

selection.when: Looking at a rendered page before pushing it: a layout, an anchor, a generated index.
selection.limits: Not what CI builds: it uses the installed just-the-docs gem rather than the pinned remote theme, so chrome can differ, while Liquid and kramdown do not. It runs the cheap post-Jekyll steps and names the rest it skipped. Read a layout question off the staging preview.
selection.cost: Local Ruby and Jekyll; a minute or two.
